name: State Board
description: Each Indian state and union territory operates its own State Board of Education, which designs the curriculum, conducts examinations, and regulates school education within the state.

name: Board of Secondary Education, Andhra Pradesh (BSEAP)
description: Advantages of the AP State Board include affordable education, wide reach across the state, and inclusion of local culture. However, like many state boards, it faces challenges such as variability in quality, infrastructure gaps, and the need for greater alignment with national educational standards.

name: Directorate of School Education, Arunachal Pradesh (DSEAP)
description: Arunachal Pradesh is a relatively young state in terms of educational development, it often aligns its curriculum and guidelines with national frameworks such as the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) to ensure quality and consistency.

name: Board of Secondary Education, Assam (SEBA)
description: SEBA designs its own curriculum, syllabus, and textbooks, with a focus on providing education that reflects Assamese language, culture, and heritage, alongside national academic standards. The board offers instruction in Assamese, English, Bengali, Bodo, and other regional languages to cater to the state’s diverse population.

name: Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB)
description: The Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) is the state education board of Bihar, responsible for conducting school examinations at the secondary (Class 10) and senior secondary (Class 12) levels. Established under the Bihar School Examination Board Act, 1952, the BSEB operates under the Government of Bihar.

name: Chhattisgarh Board of Secondary Education (CGBSE)
description: The board designs the curriculum, textbooks, and conducts important public examinations like the High School (10th) and Higher Secondary (12th) board exams. CGBSE aims to provide quality education in line with the cultural, linguistic, and educational needs of Chhattisgarh. The medium of instruction is primarily Hindi, though English-medium options are also available.

name: Goa Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (GBSHSE)
description: The Goa Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (GBSHSE) is the educational board responsible for managing secondary and higher secondary education in the state of Goa, India. Established in 1975, GBSHSE operates under the supervision of the Goa state government.

name: Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSEB)
description: The Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSEB) is the education board responsible for managing school education in the state of Gujarat, India. Established in 1960, GSEB operates under the jurisdiction of the Government of Gujarat.

name: Board of School Education Haryana (BSEH)
description: The Board of School Education Haryana (BSEH), established in 1969, is the state education board responsible for regulating and supervising school education in Haryana.The board also prescribes the curriculum, textbooks, and teaching standards for schools affiliated with it, covering subjects in English, Hindi, and other streams

name: Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education (HPBOSE)
description: The Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education (HPBOSE) is the state education board of Himachal Pradesh, established in 1969, with its headquarters in Dharamshala. HPBOSE is responsible for conducting school examinations, developing curriculum, and regulating education for both government and private schools affiliated with the board across the state.

name: Jharkhand Academic Council (JAC)
description: The Jharkhand Academic Council (JAC) is the official state education board of Jharkhand, established in 2003 after the formation of the state. Headquartered in Ranchi, JAC is responsible for overseeing school education and conducting examinations for secondary (Class 10) and higher secondary (Class 12) levels in Jharkhand.

name: Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB)
description: The Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board (KSEEB) is the state education board of Karnataka, established in 1966. It is responsible for regulating and supervising secondary education in the state, primarily conducting the SSLC (Secondary School Leaving Certificate) examination for Class 10 students

name: Kerala Board of Public Examinations (KBPE)
description: The Kerala Board of Public Examinations (KBPE) is the state education authority responsible for conducting public examinations in the state of Kerala. It operates under the Department of General Education, Government of Kerala. KBPE oversees the conduct of major exams such as the SSLC (Secondary School Leaving Certificate) for Class 10 and other public examinations in the state.

name: Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education (MPBSE)
description: The Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education (MPBSE) is the state education board of Madhya Pradesh, established in 1965 and headquartered in Bhopal. MPBSE is responsible for prescribing the curriculum, conducting examinations, and regulating the functioning of schools affiliated to it across the state.

name: Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE)

Headquartered in Pune, the board is responsible for regulating and supervising secondary (Class 10) and higher secondary (Class 12) education in Maharashtra.

name: Board of Secondary Education, Manipur (BSEM)
description: BSEM conducts the High School Leaving Certificate (HSLC) examination at the end of Class X. This examination is crucial for students as it determines their eligibility for higher secondary education.

name: Meghalaya Board of School Education (MBOSE)

It is responsible for regulating, supervising, and developing school education in the state. MBOSE conducts key examinations such as the Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) for Class 10 and the Higher Secondary School Leaving Certificate (HSSLC) for Class 12.

name: Mizoram Board of School Education (MBSE)
description: The Mizoram Board of School Education (MBSE) is the official education board of the state of Mizoram, established in 1975. It is responsible for regulating and supervising school education in Mizoram, including the development of curriculum, textbooks, and conducting examinations for secondary (Class 10) and higher secondary (Class 12) levels.

name: Nagaland Board of School Education (NBSE)
description: The Nagaland Board of School Education (NBSE) is the state education board of Nagaland, established in 1973. It is responsible for regulating, supervising, and developing school education in the state from secondary (Class 9 and 10) to higher secondary levels (Class 11 and 12). NBSE conducts key examinations such as the Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) and the Higher Secondary School Leaving Certificate (HSSLC).

name: Punjab School Education Board (PSEB)
description: The Punjab School Education Board (PSEB) is the state education board of Punjab, established in 1969 and headquartered in Mohali. PSEB is responsible for regulating school education in Punjab, including designing curriculum, prescribing textbooks, and conducting examinations for secondary (Class 10) and higher secondary (Class 12) levels

name: Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan (RBSE)

It is the main education board in the state of Rajasthan responsible for regulating, supervising, and developing secondary and higher secondary education.

name: Tamil Nadu State Board of School Examination (TNBS)
description: The Tamil Nadu State Board of School Examination is the official education board for school-level education in the state of Tamil Nadu. It is responsible for designing the curriculum, prescribing textbooks, conducting examinations, and regulating schools affiliated with it across the state.

name: Telangana State Board of Secondary Education (BSE Telangana)

Established after the formation of Telangana state in 2014, BSE Telangana conducts the important Class 10 (SSC) public examinations and oversees the curriculum, syllabus, and academic standards for schools affiliated with it.

name: Tripura Board of Secondary Education (TBSE)
description: The Tripura Board of Secondary Education (TBSE) is the state education board of Tripura, established in 1973. TBSE is responsible for regulating and developing secondary and higher secondary education in the state. It conducts major examinations such as the Class 10 (Secondary) and Class 12 (Higher Secondary) board exams for schools affiliated with it.

name: Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad (UPMSP)
description: The Uttar Pradesh Board of High School and Intermediate Education (UP Board), established in 1921, is one of the largest and oldest education boards in India. It is responsible for conducting secondary (Class 10) and higher secondary (Class 12) examinations in the state of Uttar Pradesh.

name: Uttarakhand Board of School Education (UBSE)
description: The Uttarakhand Board of School Education (UBSE) was established in 2001 after the formation of the state of Uttarakhand. It is responsible for regulating and supervising school education in Uttarakhand from the secondary (Class 10) to higher secondary (Class 12) level. UBSE designs the curriculum, prescribes textbooks, and conducts board examinations such as the Class 10 (High School) and Class 12 (Intermediate) exams.

name: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE)
description: The West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE) was established in 1951 and is responsible for overseeing secondary education (up to Class 10) in the state of West Bengal. The board regulates and supervises schools affiliated with it, designs the curriculum, prescribes textbooks, and conducts the Madhyamik Pariksha (Class 10 board examination), which is a major academic milestone for students in the state.

name: Board of Secondary Education, Odisha (BSE Odisha)

Established in 1953, the board conducts the High School Certificate (HSC) examination for Class 10 students. BSE Odisha designs the curriculum, prescribes textbooks, and regulates schools affiliated with it across the state.
